name: Taking of the Hualapai (Walapai) country without a treaty of purchase (Royce Area 683)
aka: Royce 683, Walapai: country claimed by them at beginning of their relations with the U.S.
citation: No treaty or statute: Royce records that no treaty of purchase was ever made and that the United States assumed title to their country
nations: Hualapai Tribe of the Hualapai Reservation, Arizona (Walapai)
promises: Not a treaty. Royce records that no treaty of purchase was ever made with the Hualapai and that the United States assumed title to their country, shown on his Arizona map No. 1.
Royce notes that the United States afterwards set apart a reserve for them by Executive order of January 4, 1883.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission held that the Hualapai had Indian title to the land in its Finding 17 and that the United States extinguished that title outside the Hualapai Reservation on January 4, 1883, the day it set the reservation aside, without paying for it.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Hualapai Tribe v. United States, Docket 90, Interlocutory Order, 11 Ind. Cl. Comm. 447 (1962)

source.title: Hualapai Tribe v. United States, Docket 90, Interlocutory Order (November 19, 1962), 11 Ind. Cl. Comm. 447
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.quote: the United States extinguished without the payment of compensation said Indian title

breaches.what: The Commission found the Hualapai aboriginal land outside the reservation comprised 4,459,500 acres worth $2,800,000.00 on January 4, 1883, acquired without payment, and held the tribe entitled to that sum less allowable offsets.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Docket 90, Second Interlocutory Order, 17 Ind. Cl. Comm. 456 (1966)

breaches.what: Dockets 90 and 122 were consolidated and all Hualapai claims in them were settled by compromise for $2,950,000. A settlement is not a further finding.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Dockets 90 and 122, Final Judgment (1968)

source.title: Hualapai Tribe v. United States, Dockets 90 and 122, Final Judgment (June 18, 1968), 19 Ind. Cl. Comm. 161
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

landTaken: 4,459,500 acres of Hualapai aboriginal land outside the reservation (finding 20), valued at $2,800,000.00 as of January 4, 1883 (Second Interlocutory Order, 1966).
compensation: $2,950,000 by compromise final judgment of June 18, 1968, settling all claims in Dockets 90 and 122.
today: The 1968 judgment settled all claims in both dockets. Whether and how it was distributed was not traced.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not a date of this taking. Royce 683 is undated and printed under 'Cessions of 1886' after the Pueblo grants headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress'. The Commission dated the taking January 4, 1883. Not edited.
What Docket 122 claimed was not read. The Hualapai Tribe's own history page (hualapai-nsn.gov) returned 404; the nation voice is missing.
2026-11-08: counted once with cession-1883-01-04-walapai (the Hualapai taking (Docket 90) is dated by the Jan 4, 1883 order). The map still shows this row.

Audit 2026-11-08: Docket 90 orders of 1962 and 1966 and the 1968 final judgment re-read; findings, acreage 4,459,500, value $2,800,000.00 and the $2,950,000 compromise match, and the quote is exact. Removed stale notes: treaties.json now lists the Hualapai, and cession-1883-01-04-walapai has a findings file (this file points to it).

plain.promised: Nothing. No treaty of purchase was made. The United States assumed title to the Hualapai country and set apart a reservation in 1883.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found the United States took 4,459,500 acres of Hualapai land outside the reservation on January 4, 1883 without paying, and valued it at $2,800,000.00.
plain.today: All Hualapai claims in the two dockets were settled in 1968 for $2,950,000. Whether the money was distributed was not traced.
